newsitem.title: FRANCE: French appeals jails Iranians for "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: French appeals jails Iranians for "terrorism".

text.p: A French appeals court upheld on Friday prison sentences levelled last year against two men for supplying Iran's secret services with information aimed at helping to kill opponents in France.
Mojtaba Mashhady, 39, a French citizen of Iranian origin, was jailed for seven years. Iranian Hossein Yasdenseta, 37, was given a three-year sentence.
Both were found guilty of conspiring towards terrorism.

The decision came after a Berlin court found on April 10 that Iranian leaders ordered the murders of three Kurdish dissidents, a ruling which led most European Union countries to withdraw their ambassadors from Tehran and drop the policy of dialogue.
Mashhady and Yasdenseta are also being investigated by anti-terrorist magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere in connection with the killing of Iranian dissident Cyrus Elahi in Paris in 1990.
The appeals court ordered them to pay the symbolic figure of one franc in damages to civil plaintiffs SOS Attentats (SOS Attacks), a private association grouping victims of bomb attacks in France.
The association said in a statement the appeals court ruling "again exposed the terrorist nature of the Iranian regime and its leaders".
It urged the European Union to threaten Tehran with economic sanctions unless it ends "terror activities" and lifts its order to kill British writer Salman Rushdie for allegedly blaspheming Islam.
Senior U.S. official Peter Tarnoff toured major West European capitals earlier this week to try to persuade European countries to join the U.S. hard line against Iran.

The State Department had said that although Washington's "ideal scenario" would be for the Europeans to adopt the same trade sanctions against Iran as the United States has done, it doubted that was realistic.
